name: Durry Kwain
subtitle: Ice cream. Memories. A hallway that is negotiating.
description:
The sign says DURRY KWAIN in letters the colour of a boiled sweet, and the man inside says his own name the same way, and neither of them will tell you which came first. Silvora Reefs does not regard this as a question.

Inside: gingham, chrome, the particular under-hum of a freezer working hard in a warm room, and the smell of vanilla laid over something colder and further off. The hallway to the back stretches or does not stretch depending on the hour and on nothing else you have been able to isolate. The menu board is chalk. The chalk changes. Tonight it is offering a Schrödinger's Sundae — both chocolate and vanilla until served — at a price that has three decimal places.
revisit:
Darek has the cone made before the bell over the door has finished moving. He does this every time, and he does it without looking up, and the timing is so consistent that you have twice come in intending to order nothing at all and both times left holding something you did in fact want.

The freezer is working hard in a warm room. The chalk board has revised itself since Tuesday. The hallway to the back is whatever length it is this evening, and Darek carries a mop through it twice a night and has never once remarked on the distance.

lucid.2: The freezer hum has a rhythm under it that is not a compressor. Compressors do not pause to think.
lucid.4: Darek is not answering ahead of your questions. Darek is answering on time, to a script that has your lines in it as well as his, and he has never once had cause to notice the difference.

ambient: The chalk board revises itself while your back is turned. The new item is spelled correctly and priced to three decimal places, and the correct spelling is somehow the unnerving part.

A child at the window table takes a spoonful, stops, and goes somewhere for about four seconds — eyes open, spoon halfway down, entirely absent. Then comes back, and keeps eating, and nobody at the table remarks on it because nobody at the table has noticed, because it happens to all of them.

The hallway to the back has grown by about a third since you sat down. Darek does not look up. Darek has never once looked up for this, in eleven years, and the mop goes through it at the same pace it always does.

The freezer hum drops a tone and holds there, working at something, and then comes back up. In the gap there is another sound underneath it, patient and rhythmic, and it stops the moment you turn your head toward it.
Somebody outside goes past the window at a pace that does not match the weather, twice, in the same direction.

objects.name: the chalk menu board
objects.description:
Six flavours, three sizes, one special. The hand is Darek's, patient and looping, and the special tonight is SCHRÖDINGER'S SUNDAE — BOTH CHOC & VAN UNTIL SERVED — 3.331.

Underneath, in the corner where a board usually says CLOSED SUNDAYS, it says: THANK YOU FOR YOUR PATIENCE. WE APOLOGISE FOR THE WAIT. It has said this for as long as you have been coming here. There has never been a wait. Durry Kwain has never once had a queue.
objects.repeat: The special has changed again — a new name, a new price, the same three decimal places. The apology in the corner has not changed. It has not changed once in eleven years, and it is the only line on this board written in a hand that is not quite Darek's.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the prices are not prices. 3.331 is a timestamp with the colon taken out, and it is thirty-one seconds after your watch stopped, and every other price on the board is a different second of the same minute.

passive.text: Three decimal places on an ice cream board. 3.331. Your watch has been stopped at 3:33 since before you can date, and it is stopped at thirty-one seconds past, and it is on your wrist right now. That is not a price. Somebody has been pricing this shop in your watch, in chalk, in public, for years.

'We apologise for the wait,' on a board belonging to a shop that has never overseen a wait, in a hand that is not quite the hand that wrote the flavours. That is not customer service and it is not politeness. That is a line of dialogue left in from a draft where there *was* a queue, and nobody has been back to take it out.

clue.title: Everything is priced at 3:33
clue.text: Durry Kwain's prices run to three decimal places and every one of them is a second inside the minute at which your watch stopped.

check.prompt: The board is chalk and the names on it have been written over often enough that the surface is more ghost than slate. Take the names apart properly — not what they sell, what they *meant* before somebody made them into flavours.
check.success:
Durry Kwain. Durian. *Do rry qu'un* — and under that, older, a phrase that means roughly 'only the one is permitted'.

Every flavour on this board is a variation on a single word, and the word is not a flavour. It is a restriction, and somebody has been advertising it in chalk for eleven years and calling it dessert.
check.failure:
Durry. Kwain. You turn them over and they come apart into syllables that mean nothing much and reassemble into the same two words, smug about it, refusing to be anything but a shop.

The chalk has been rewritten so many times that the board is mostly the ghosts of previous boards, and the ghosts are in no language you can get hold of tonight, at this temperature, with a man watching you kindly from behind the counter.

clue.title: Only the one is permitted
clue.text: Every flavour name at Durry Kwain is a variation on one older phrase meaning 'only the one is permitted'. It is a rule advertised as a menu.

objects.name: the hallway to the back
objects.description:
It goes from the end of the counter to a door marked STAFF, and it is either eleven feet long or thirty-odd, and it has been both this evening.

The interesting part is not the length. The interesting part is the skirting board, which runs the whole way in a single unbroken length of moulding, with no join, in a hallway that has been three different lengths since you sat down. Whatever is doing this is doing it to the moulding too, and doing it well, and doing it with an attention to continuity that suggests somebody would be embarrassed to be caught out.
objects.repeat: Longer than it was. The moulding is still one unbroken length with no join in it anywhere, at whatever distance the hallway has decided on this time, and somebody is still being extremely careful about a detail that nobody in this shop has ever looked at twice.
objects.monocle: The gold shows you the hallway at all its lengths at once, stacked like pages held up to a lamp — and in the margin of each one, faint, a number. They are not consecutive. They go 41, 41, 42, 41. Somebody keeps going back to 41.

passive.text:
Pace it. Fourteen steps out, fourteen steps back, and the fourteenth lands against the same scuff in the skirting both times, at both lengths, on a night when the hallway has been three different distances.

It is not the hallway that is changing length. It is your account of the hallway, and the scuff is where the account is nailed down at both ends.

check.prompt: Walk it while watching the skirting rather than the door. The trick with a continuity error is never to look at the place the continuity is being kept — look at the thing nobody thought you would check.
check.success:
You keep your eyes on the skirting and walk, and at the eighth step the moulding does something that furniture does not do: it *extends*, without joining, the way a line extends when a hand draws more of it.

At the ninth step there is a hand. Not in the hallway. In the periphery of the hallway, at the level where a margin would be, holding nothing and resting.
check.failure:
You watch the moulding and the moulding is a moulding. Fourteen steps, a door marked STAFF, a smell of cold air and vanilla, and behind you Darek saying 'Sorry about your wait' to a room in which you are the only customer and have waited for precisely nothing.

Whatever the hallway does, it declines to do it while being watched by a man who has decided to watch it.

clue.title: A hand in the margin
clue.text: Watching the skirting rather than the door, the hallway extends the way a drawn line extends. There is a hand at the level where a margin would be.

objects.name: the Schrödinger's Sundae
objects.description:
Darek makes it without being asked, because Darek makes everything without being asked, and sets it down with a napkin folded into the shape of nothing in particular.

It is both chocolate and vanilla. Not swirled — both, in the same volume, at the same time, in a way the eye keeps trying to resolve into stripes and cannot. The spoon is already in it. Silvora Reefs ice cream carries other people's memories; that is not a rumour, it is a menu item, and Reefers order by which memory they are in the mood for.
objects.repeat: There is another one on the counter. Darek does not charge for the second and never has, and you have never worked out how to ask why without it becoming a conversation neither of you wants to have.
objects.monocle: Through the gold there is no ice cream in the dish. There is a paragraph, folded into a cold shape, and the first line of it is one you recognise from a page in your notebook that is not wet.

check.prompt: It is free, it is cold, it is the only uncomplicated thing that has happened to you since the water. It is also a Silvora Reefs memory-bearing confection served by a man who is running a touch previous, which means it is none of those things. Eat it anyway.
check.success:
Cold, then sweet, then somewhere else.

You are eight. It is a kitchen you have not stood in since your parents were alive in it, and your mother is at the table painting something with her back to you, and she says, without turning, 'And furthermore—'

She says it in your voice. She says the whole line in your voice, the cadence and the shrug at the end, and she is not a woman doing an impression of her son, she is a woman reading a line that was written for her.

The kitchen goes. The dish is empty. Darek is wiping the counter and says, 'Sorry about your wait,' and this time the timing is exactly right, and that is worse.
check.failure: Cold, then sweet, then somewhere else, and the somewhere else does not resolve. Fragments arrive out of order and refuse to assemble: a kitchen, a green lamp, an apology, a woman's back. You come out of it holding the spoon too hard, with the taste of somebody else's childhood in your mouth and a headache arriving on schedule.

clue.title: Your mother, reading
clue.text: A memory in the ice cream: your mother, at a table, saying 'And furthermore—' in your voice and your cadence. Not an impression. A reading.

objects.name: the freezer cabinet
objects.description:
Chrome, misted glass, nine tubs. The labels are handwritten on tape and several of them are not flavours: HER LAST SUMMER. THE DOG, BEFORE. AN AFTERNOON NOBODY CLAIMED.

The ninth tub has no label. It has never had a label. It is the only one that is full to the rim, and the surface of it is perfectly flat, unserved, untouched — nine tubs in a busy shop and one of them has never been sold from.
objects.repeat: Still nine tubs. Still eight labels and one blank. The ninth is still full to the rim with a surface so flat it might have been poured this morning, and Darek's hand still goes from the eighth to the counter without pausing where the ninth would be.
objects.monocle: The gold gives the ninth tub a label after all. It is your handwriting, and it says LATER, and the word has been written and struck out and written again four times, each time slightly further to the left, as though the label were being retyped by somebody who kept mistaking the margin.

passive.text: Darek is not avoiding the ninth tub. That is the thing to get right, because avoidance would be a kind of knowledge. Watch his hand: it goes from the eighth to the counter in one movement, at speed, without the fractional hesitation of a man declining to look at something. There is no ninth tub in the world his hand is moving through.

clue.title: LATER
clue.text: The unlabelled ninth tub carries, under the monocle, a label in your handwriting reading LATER — struck out and rewritten four times, each time further into the margin.

check.prompt: The cabinet has not been opened in some time and has no intention of starting now. The seal has gone stiff and the hinge has gone stiffer. Open it anyway, with the shoulder if necessary.
check.success:
The seal gives with a sound like a held breath being returned. Inside, in rows, in the cold: not tubs.

Jars. Nineteen of them, lidded and labelled, and every label is a date, and every date is in the future.
check.failure: It is a door and you are a man and the door wins, twice. The second time something in the right shoulder makes a note of the exchange and files it with the others, and the cabinet stands there with its nine tubs behind misted glass, entirely unbothered, as it has stood since before your father would have been born.

clue.title: Nineteen jars, dated forward
clue.text: The Durry Kwain freezer holds nineteen labelled jars. Every label is a date and every date has not happened yet.

objects.name: a notice by the till
objects.description:
Framed, fly-specked, and hung at the height of a man who did not want it read. A trading licence, issued to DUR. KWAIN (SOLE PROP.), and stamped in the bottom corner with four lobes you have started to recognise.

Beneath the seal, in print small enough to constitute an opinion: PREMISES ASSESSED. DIMENSIONAL VARIANCE WITHIN PERMITTED TOLERANCE. PROPRIETOR NOT TO BE INFORMED.
objects.repeat: You have read it four times now and the last line has been the last line every time, which you have started checking for, which is itself a thing worth noticing about the state of you this evening.

passive.text: Somebody measured this hallway. Somebody found it varying, wrote the variance down, assessed it against a tolerance that must therefore exist in a document somewhere, found it acceptable, and then specifically instructed that the man who works in it not be told. Four decisions. Every one of them made by a person, in an office, on a form.

'Proprietor not to be informed.' That is not secrecy — secrecy is cheaper and does not require a line in a public document. That is somebody deciding what Darek can carry, and deciding it protectively, and putting it in writing where anybody who ever bothered to read a licence would find it.

clue.title: Dimensional variance, permitted
clue.text: The Quad-C has measured Durry Kwain's hallway, found it varying, permitted the variance, and directed that Darek not be told.

check.prompt: A notice by the till: laminated, ordinary, hand-washing. Ignore the notice. Read the *board* it is pinned to.
check.success:
The notice is nothing. The *board* is the thing: four pin-holes at the corners of a rectangle that is not this notice's rectangle, and a rectangle of unfaded paint inside it.

Something larger hung here for years and came down recently, and the man behind the counter has put a laminated card about hand-washing over the gap.
check.failure: Opening hours, an allergy warning, and a hand-washing instruction with a cartoon on it that has been there long enough for the cartoon to have gone yellow. You read all three twice and they go on being exactly and only what they are.

clue.title: A rectangle of unfaded paint
clue.text: The notice board at Durry Kwain has pin-holes and unfaded paint from something much larger that was removed recently and covered over.

exits.hang_hi: back up the hill to a floor that hangs from nothing
exits.mobius: the harbour road, and the sign that is a joke about surfaces
exits.rest_assured: the long climb to the obsidian
exits.dudes_dews: along past the green lamps to the queue that never stops moving
exits.cheeses_thrice: down the narrow street toward an oven and a great deal of feeling
